item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Public Advisory Number 7
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM GMT Mon Sep 21 2026 
349 
WTNT31 KNHC 210237
TCPAT1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Fay Advisory Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
300 AM GMT Mon Sep 21 2026
 
...FAY NEARLY A HURRICANE BUT FORECAST TO WEAKEN ON MONDAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 AM GMT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...34.1N 31.9W
ABOUT 385 MI...620 KM SW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...70 MPH...110 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...ESE OR 120 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...995 MB...29.39 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 AM GMT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Fay was 
located near latitude 34.1 North, longitude 31.9 West. Fay is now 
moving toward the east-southeast near 5 mph (7 km/h). A turn to the 
southwest is anticipated on Monday which should continue through the 
early part of this week.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 70 mph (110 km/h)
with higher gusts. Little change is strength is forecast tonight,
but Fay should begin to weaken on Monday. The tropical cyclone is
forecast to become a post-tropical cyclone by the middle of this
week.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles (130 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 995 mb (29.39 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 AM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Forecast Discussion Number 7
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM GMT Mon Sep 21 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 210240
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Storm Fay Discussion Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
300 AM GMT Mon Sep 21 2026
 
Fay is beginning to feel the effects of increasing northwesterly
shear over its circulation, with satellite images showing its
outflow pattern becoming restricted in that quadrant. However, an
ASCAT-C pass received after the prior advisory showed a peak wind
retrieval of 53 kt, and that the center was a little further south
and east of what was previously estimated. Assuming some wind
undersampling of this instrument along with a slight increase in the
DMINT and DPRINT intensity estimates, the initial intensity is being
nudged up to 60 kt for this advisory, making Fay just shy of
hurricane intensity.
 
Fay appears to have turned east-southeastward tonight, with an
estimated motion of 130/4 kt. Over the next day or so, a building
ridge to the northwest should continue to turn Fay southward and
then southwestward with gradually increasing forward motion. The NHC
track forecast this cycle was shifted a bit southward compared to
the previous one, but converges close to the previous forecast
track in 60-72 h. This track forecast remains in good agreement with
the reliable HFIP Corrected Consensus Approach (HCCA) and Google
DeepMind ensemble mean (GDMI) aids.
 
The tropical storm is just about out of time to intensify further,
though it remains possible Fay could briefly become a hurricane
tonight before the northwesterly vertical wind shear becomes
prohibitively strong from an amplifying upper-level ridge to the
northwest. This shear will ultimately import very dry mid-level air
into Fay's core, causing the cyclone to quickly decouple in the
next 24-36 h. The global and hurricane-regional model guidance
remains in good agreement on Fay struggling to produce organized
convection by 48-60 h, and that continues to be when the NHC
forecast indicates the cyclone becoming post-tropical. The NHC
intensity forecast is largely an update of the prior one beyond the
next 12 h, in good agreement with the intensity aid consensus.
